chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ، رَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who narrated it from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قِيلَ لَهُ: إِنَّ رَجُلًا تَزَوَّجَ بِجَارِيَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ فَأَرْضَعَتْهَا امْرَأَتُهُ، ثُمَّ أَرْضَعَتْهَا امْرَأَةٌ لَهُ أُخْرَى، فَقَالَ ابْنُ شُبْرُمَةَ: حَرُمَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَامْرَأَتَاهُ، فَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: أَخْطَأَ ابْنُ شُبْرُمَةَ، حَرُمَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَامْرَأَتُهُ الَّتِي أَرْضَعَتْهَا أَوَّلًا، فَأَمَّا الْآخِرَةُ فَلَمْ تَحْرُمْ عَلَيْهِ، كَأَنَّهَا أَرْضَعَتْ ابْنَتَهُ

translations.en: It was said to him: A man married a young girl, and his wife breastfed her, then another wife of his breastfed her. Ibn Shubruma said: The girl and both his wives are prohibited to him. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Ibn Shubruma erred; the girl and the wife who breastfed her first are prohibited to him, but as for the latter, she is not prohibited to him, as if she had breastfed his daughter.

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of 'radh' (breastfeeding) in establishing marital prohibitions, specifically addressing the scenario where a man marries a young girl who is subsequently breastfed by his existing wives. It refutes Ibn Shubruma's view that all wives become prohibited, establishing instead that only the first wife who breastfed the girl creates a direct siblinghood bond, while subsequent wives' breastfeeding is treated as if they breastfed the girl's daughter, thus not creating a new prohibition for the husband. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific timing and sequence of breastfeeding events in determining kinship ties.
en.seo_question: How does the order of breastfeeding affect marital prohibitions in Shia fiqh?
